title: Fidelity-tiered autoscaler and lane-transition model (PRD sketch)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This doc sketches a fidelity-tiered autoscaling model for Dedicated capacity that combines predictable reserved capacity, short-term runway credits for bursts, and controlled lane transitions between high-fidelity (low-latency, higher-cost) and low-fidelity (batch/quantized, higher-throughput) execution lanes. The goal is to give customers deterministic latency/cost profiles while enabling short bursts and graceful spillover under contention, with explicit tenant isolation boundaries.

Why this is different / problem statement:
- Current Dedicated autoscaling proposals focus on pool sizing, soft prewarm and simple burst credits. They lack an integrated concept of "fidelity" — the observable tradeoffs between latency, compute intensity, and cost — and explicit transitions between runtime lanes.
- Customers want predictable SLOs but also business-case bursts (marketing launches, daily batch spikes) without paying for permanently provisioned excess.
- Operators need a compact set of knobs for fairness, isolation, and predictable billing during lane transitions.

High-level proposal overview:
1) Lanes (runtime fidelity tiers):
   - fidelity:high (interactive): pinned GPUs, prewarmed KV cache, strict latency SLO (e.g., p95 < 300ms). Higher cost-profile.
   - fidelity:balanced (mixed): elastic nodes with partial prewarm, quantized kernels allowed, p95 target relaxed (e.g., p95 < 700ms).
   - fidelity:low (batch/throughput): aggressive quantization, async response patterns, high batching allowed, best-effort latency.

2) Runway credits and short-burst currency:
   - Each tenant has a runway budget (seconds-of-high-fidelity or tokens-of-hottime) that can be consumed for short bursts into fidelity:high beyond their reserved share.
   - Runway decays over time and can be refilled by committed reserve purchases or earned via usage patterns.
   - Credit consumption triggers telemetry events and optional customer alerts.

3) Predictive autoscaler that understands fidelity:
   - Uses arrival-rate + sequence-length distribution + model-size to predict token/sec demand across lanes.
   - When forecasted demand exceeds reserved capacity, the autoscaler evaluates: 1) move some low-priority traffic to fidelity:low/balanced, 2) borrow runway credits, 3) spin ephemeral balanced nodes (fast ramp), 4) as last resort, reject or queue.

4) Lane-transition mechanics and policies:
   - Transitions are explicit policy objects per tenant: e.g., "preferred_lane_order": [high, balanced, low], plus conditional thresholds like p99 latency > X or runway below Y.
   - Transition actions: warm KV caches (partial), swap kernels to more quantized paths, change batching windows, fallback to smaller model variant.
   - All transitions are reversible; cooling windows and hysteresis are configurable to avoid oscillation.

5) Isolation controls and fairness:
   - Tenants can opt into stricter isolation: guaranteed slices of high fidelity capacity that do not accept runway borrowing.
   - Soft-isolation mode: loaned runway from pool subject to global fairness policy (proportional to subscription tier).
   - Preemption rules: higher SLA tenants can preempt runway or get priority in lane promotion; system logs and audit trails record preempts.

Config sketch (human-readable example) :
- tenant-config: {
    reserved_high: 3 nodes,
    runway_seconds: 900,
    preferred_lane_order: [high, balanced, low],
    isolation_mode: soft
  }

Operational flows (examples):
- Normal steady-state: traffic served in high until reserved_high saturated; autoscaler keeps balanced pool minimal for latency smoothing.
- Short marketing surge: tenant consumes runway for 12 minutes; runway drops, alerts fire at 50% consumption; when runway exhausted, traffic either moves to balanced (degraded latency) or is rate-limited depending on policy.
- Prolonged spike: autoscaler predicts >10min sustained excess; spins balanced nodes and recommends tenant to purchase temporary reserved uplift (UI CTA + billing link).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Autoscaler can predict and trigger lane transitions in a staging tenant replay test (deterministic scenarii).
- Runway credit ledger records consumption events and refills; UI shows current runway and projected depletion at current rate.
- Latency SLOs for fidelity:high maintained for reserved capacity under 95% load.
- No silent cross-tenant preemption: all preemptions generate audit logs and customer-visible notifications.

Key metrics to ship with MVP:
- P95 and P99 latency per lane and per-tenant
- Runway consumption (seconds/minute) and refill rate
- Frequency and duration of lane transitions per tenant
- Preemption events (count, affected requests)
- Cost delta (CPU/GPU hours) vs prior autoscaler baseline

Security and billing notes:
- Bill runway consumption as a separate line-item so customers can see cost of bursts.
- Ensure private deployments honor KMS and network rules while performing lane transitions; no external callbacks during transitions.

Rollout plan and safety gates:
1) Lab tests with synthetic traffic and sequence-length variance.
2) Canary with 3 friendly customers under opt-in flags; monitor preemption and runway billing UX.
3) Gradual ramp to all Dedicated tenants with conservative defaults (runway small, preemption disabled).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantified pricing model for runway units (flat rate vs usage-weighted).
- Acceptable hysteresis windows for lane transitions to avoid oscillation across a fleet of tenants.
- How to represent multi-model workloads where different models have different fidelity/sensitivity.
- Interaction with Dedicated SLA contracts (billing credits if runway preempted).

Next steps (short-term):
- Engineering spike: simulator to model runway economics and latency tradeoffs (owner: Ravi)
- Instrumentation plan: events and traces for lane transitions (owner: Lina)
- UX draft: runway panel and per-tenant policy editor (owner: Maya)

Notes / references:
- Related tickets: JIRA DED-8921 (autoscale forecasting), DED-9010 (billing runway).
- See CONFLUENCE:INFR-1234 for kernel-selection constraints and GITHUB:repo/PR#1602 for early autoscaler code.

Quick checklist for first engineering milestone:
- [ ] Basic lane definitions wired into orchestrator
- [ ] Runway ledger and simple billing hook
- [ ] Predictive autoscaler prototype + offline replay experiments
- [ ] Small canary with opt-in toggle + telemetry dashboards
